analysis: The trial completed successfully but did not improve validation: pinned-host macro HR@10 was 0.5000 versus the supplied prior 0.5237, a decline of 0.0237. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.550, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.580, Electronics 0.340, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.530. Electronics declined from the reported prior 0.365 and remained below its reported SASRec baseline of 0.420. These results do not support replacing uniform preference pooling with this learned exponential pooling configuration. The cause is unresolved: learned decay values and training curves were not supplied, so excessive recency weighting or optimization effects remain hypotheses. Host validation, rather than hidden test performance, supports these conclusions.
code_summary: One independent ConvRec model per category uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, eight causal residual convolution blocks with dilations (1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8), and two-head causal self-attention. A parallel internal preference pathway computes normalized causal exponential pooling of raw embeddings using one jointly learned scalar decay initialized to a 20-position half-life. Projected, normalized preferences fuse with sequence features through a learned gate before final normalization and item-embedding scoring with a trained item bias. Training retains 32-negative cross-entropy, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, seed 42, and validation checkpoint selection. The predictor strictly loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, including log_decay, with shared history packing and dataset routing. Included diagnostics check causality, finite empty-history outputs, gradients, and checkpoint reload parity while preserving training RNG state.
